children: app Muse has gained more than 3.4M downloads in the U.S. and Canada since its launch on Sept. 8, according to Sensor Tower data, as personalized AI apps gain traction with consumers.
Sensor Tower estimates Muse had 2.8M downloads globally in its first two weeks, compared with 3.7M for ChatGPT
during their respective first two weeks.
Muse reached No. 1 on the U.S. Apple App Store on Sept. 18 and also topped the U.S. Google Play Store the following day. It remained No. 1 on both stores as of Thursday.
Meta’s ability to promote Muse across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp may have helped drive its early growth, Sensor Tower said.
Muse accounted for the largest share of Meta’s in-house advertising impressions within 10 days of its launch, ahead of those platforms, according to the research firm.

Elon Musk’s Grok Bot has also continued to grow despite Muse’s launch. The app has recorded 2.2M global downloads since its August launch and averaged about 300,000 daily active users as of Sept. 22, Sensor Tower estimated.

Grok Bot’s daily active users rose 43% in the week ended Sept. 21. Its downloads and daily active users increased 134% and 164%, respectively, in the two weeks through Sept. 21 from the previous two-week period.
Sensor Tower said Grok Bot has generated more than $1M in subscription revenue, suggesting some users are willing to pay for AI services that offer more personalized features.
"AI could become more tailored to individual users as the market matures," Sensor Tower said.

title: Meta’s Muse gains ground as personalized AI apps grow
